problem: It says starting at Ethereum in 2015 'skips roughly seven years of working Bitcoin history'. The working ledger began with the genesis block on 3 January 2009, so 2009 to 2015 is six years by the chapter's own year-counting convention (used in Worked example 2 and Quiz Q5). The 'seven years' figure belongs to the whitepaper (2008), not to the running network.
fix: Starting blockchain history at Ethereum in 2015, which skips about six years of working Bitcoin history (seven if you count from the October 2008 whitepaper).

problem: It states 'the genesis block followed 1 year later in 2009'. That is the year difference (2009 minus 2008), but the actual elapsed time from the October 2008 whitepaper to 3 January 2009 is about three months. A student can read '1 year later' as a duration and place the genesis block in late 2009.
fix: The year difference is 1 (2008 to 2009); the actual gap is about three months, since the whitepaper came in October 2008 and the genesis block on 3 January 2009. Keep '1' only as the year-count answer.
